method: One reviewer inspects chronological half-second samples from recorded1x clips, arranged at320x180 per sample. Silent2fps thumbnails cannot establish audio quality,every fast impact or native image sharpness; quantitative timing and native screenshots are separate.

rows.name: mochi
observations: Mochi leaves the resting ring for a short forward motion, then returns; the poses differ from the circular guard and group ultimate.
Golden arched barriers and broad pale lantern/apron-like shapes recur as distinct motifs; the group peaks around5.0,11.0,16.5–17.0 and22.5seconds cover parts of allied bodies.
Gold effects share the warm stage palette and rely on brightness; the large empty rug leaves the figures small in the wide camera.
The full stage and bottom actor plates stay visible in the sampled sequence. No claim about unsampled frames or natural controller pacing.

rows.name: soot
observations: The small violet target glyph, brief pale wing/ring strike and looping outlined ultimate differ in silhouette; the 4–5s/10–11s/16–17s/22–23s sequences repeat these motifs.
Soot remains at the back-left of the allied cluster; the dark body and effects are harder to read against the warm, dark scene than Panko or Clover.

The ultimate outlines stay mostly around the target; allied bodies remain more visible than during Clover group effects. Much of each six-second cycle appears visually quiet in the half-second samples.
The target highlight and short action card help attribution, but the wide camera and large empty middle reduce face and motion readability.

rows.name: clover
observations: The basic action visibly moves Clover forward before returning; leaf-like shards, curling stems and three tall mint loops give a readable plant/healing theme.
White mint leaves and loops cover portions of the three allied bodies at 3.5/5.0/11.0/16.5–17.0/22.5s. Shape distinction is visible, but silhouettes compete during group peaks.
The back-left starting position stacks Clover close to Soot and Mochi; expressions are not legible at this thumbnail scale. Native-resolution screenshots must judge sharpness.
The three-loop group ultimate reads larger than the basic leaf strike and local curl. Repetition is a scripted gallery loop, not natural controller pacing.

rows.name: panko
observations: Panko has a distinct round warm-yellow body and twin rounded-square golden arches at 5.0/11.0/16.5–17.0/22.5s; basic forward strike and group pale patches have different silhouettes.
The ultimate frames the caster and usually preserves its face in these samples; group patches overlap allies around 3.5/9.0/15.0/21.0s.
Gold-on-wood and warm lighting limit color separation, while the pale face remains easier to pick out than Soot. A clearer value hierarchy could reduce the need for large bright outlines.
The wide fixed camera leaves the center rug mostly empty. Samples show anticipation/return poses, but 2fps cannot prove fast contact timing or continuous smoothness.

rows.name: mallow
observations: Mallow moves forward with a compact glowing ring, then uses pale peach patches and radial target marks. The ultimate begins with outlined whisk-like shapes around the caster and encloses the opponent in a tall rounded form at5.0/10.5/16.5/22.5s.
Target-side crescents and the taller enclosure differ from Panko caster-side twin arches. Both still rely on warm pale outlines against a warm room, so color alone contributes little separation.
Mallow is noticeably smaller and darker than the accompanying Mochi. Its facial performance is unreadable in these320px samples, even when the effect itself is identifiable.
The sampled ultimate often covers the target body. Landing and return poses are visible, but the silent2fps sampling cannot establish every impact beat or perceived sound quality.

rows.name: sorrel
observations: The tall leaf-like head silhouette is distinct at rest. Small curled projectiles travel toward the target, while the support action creates larger pointed pale forms over allies.
The ultimate uses a very pale teapot/leaf-shaped silhouette and coiled trails around the party at5.0/11.0/16.5–17.0/22.5s; the caster and nearby ally silhouettes merge at the brightest peaks.
Thin cyan lines contrast with the rug but are small. Similar mint tones and curled trails across Sorrel/Clover reduce distinction at thumbnail scale even though their compositions differ.
Rear-party stacking and bright flattened effects remain readability weaknesses. The samples identify pose changes but cannot establish weight, facial performance or every impact beat.

rows.name: biscuit
observations: The basic action has a visible forward travel and pale horizontal sweep; separate folding wedge/cloth forms burst at the target. The ultimate builds a larger jagged paper/pastry-like wave at5.0/11.0/16.5/22.5s.
Compared with Panko rounded arches, Biscuit uses conspicuous angular surfaces. They are readable silhouettes but large near-white faces look flat and hide portions of the enemy during peaks.
Biscuit returns to its ring between attacks, preserving the stage geography. The wide gap gives attacks travel distance but keeps the character small through much of the clip.
The timeline is an isolated four-action loop. It demonstrates distinct authored shapes and poses, not natural auto-controller pacing or uninterrupted high-frame-rate motion.

rows.name: inkcap
observations: Inkcap uses linked angular glyphs for the small projectile, a folded pale star beside the caster, and a tall ink-page enclosure that becomes a pointed fan beneath the opponent at5.0/10.5–11.0/16.5–17.0/22.5–23.0s.
The dark capped model and pale lavender effects have a distinct theme, but the character overlaps Soot in the rear party cluster and is hard to separate at rest.
The ultimate has a clearer build-and-collapse silhouette than the short projectile. Large pale planes temporarily obscure the target and have little visible surface shading in these samples.
Repeated casts preserve stage framing and readable actor plates. Half-second thumbnails are insufficient to grade fine gestures, exact contact timing or native edge quality.

rows.name: cinnamon
observations: The small attack uses travelling starbursts; support produces compact loops around allies; the ultimate has a recognizable large service-bell silhouette at4.5/10.0/16.0/22.0s.
The bell reads quickly as a cafe motif, but its bright flat face hides part of Cinnamon and the rear allied group. Smaller actions have much less screen presence.
Cinnamon remains clustered with Soot and Mochi; the wide stage makes the bell more legible than the actual actor. Gold and cream effects share the environment palette.
Repeated cycles show changes in body lean and direction. Silent half-second samples cannot establish exact beat spacing, continuous smoothness or audio quality.

rows.name: brioche
observations: Brioche has a conspicuous tall halo/head outline and pale face. Folded paper forms travel to the target; a distinct joined constellation/apron construction surrounds allies during the ultimate at4.5–5.0/10.5/16.0–16.5/22.0–22.5s.
The character silhouette is easier to separate from Soot than several smaller cats. Pose and arm changes are visible in the sampled sequence.
The group ultimate partly covers Mochi and Soot with large pale angular faces. Its connected structure is recognizable, but the flat bright rendering competes with character contours.
The large empty center persists across the loop. These authored-gallery actions establish distinct compositions, while natural fight pacing must be assessed separately in the boss recording.

rows.name: velvet
observations: Velvet produces folded lilac projectiles and a distinctive two-sided curtain shape across the opponent at4.5/10.0–10.5/16.0–16.5/22.0s. The broad rectangular silhouette differs from rings and plant loops.
The dark, slim actor has a small screen footprint and merges visually with Soot at rest. During forward travel the actor separates more clearly from the party.
The curtain nearly hides the enemy at its peak. Pale planes read more like hard paper panels than soft fabric at this scale, limiting the intended softness/weight.
Return motion and repeated stage positions are evident. This sampled gallery sequence does not establish native edge quality, smooth motion or a naturally paced fight.

rows.name: marigold
observations: The yellow floral head ornament gives Marigold a distinct outline. A pale flower projectile, curling target stems, group petals and three clear teapot silhouettes differentiate the four actions.
The group ultimate peaks around4.5/10.5/16.5/22.0–22.5s. Teapots are recognizable before large pale floral clusters partly cover the allies.
The model and effects communicate the cafe/garden theme clearly, but yellow-green and cream motifs overlap with Clover/Sorrel in the warm stage palette.
Marigold stays at the back of a tightly projected trio. Small body scale, repeated background cups and empty rug remain visible; fine expression and impact timing need native/full-frame evaluation.

rows.name: clover-ultimate
observations: The standalone ultimate repeatedly builds three tall mint loops from low leaves around the party, then dissolves back to the resting trio. The Greenhouse morning action card stays identifiable at each replay.
The large group silhouette supports the healing/plant theme, but bright leaves and loops cross nearby faces and bodies at many peaks (1.0,3.0,4.5,6.5,8.0,10.0s and later repeats).
The body contribution is mostly a compact lean/arm change behind the large effect at this wide scale. The effect is easier to read than Clover expression or weight shift.

This25s recording repeats only the gallery ultimate and preserves the account. It does not demonstrate resource timing, healing decisions or natural controller pacing; the sequence is silent2fps review.

rows.name: boss
observations: All18sheets/341half-second samples inspected chronologically, including lighting/effect preparation at0–3s, renderedstage3.5s, boss disappearing153.5s, remaining yarn adds until169.5s and Victory/MVP Soot at170s. Full recording170.4s; visible unlock grants level10/3star cats; not starter balance evidence.

Controller advances71choices and uses attacks,guard,heals,ultimates without player skill/target inputs. Boss spawns small yarn adds at18.5s and later. Soot multi-target threads, Mochi group lanterns and Clover green arches remain recognizable in natural combat.

Large central rug dominates nearly every frame. Clover and Soot cluster at rear left, while boss/add labels crowd the right. Broad pale lantern/greenhouse effects obscure allies at28,31,58,69,91.5,108,119.5,144.5and150.5s.

Looped single attacks and return-to-ring poses make the long boss fight feel repetitive. Boss falls before the small adds; the extra roughly16seconds reads as cleanup rather than a strong finishing beat.

Victory is visible in the last sample; MVP panel is oversized with much empty width and lower contribution cards below the viewport. This clip includes only a short Result glimpse; the existing three-size path screenshots cover settled result controls.

Silent2fps thumbnail review establishes broad choreography/composition and state transitions, not continuous-motion smoothness, audio quality,native sharpness or frame-time performance. Those limits apply to every clip score.
